source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why can adding many unrelated responsibilities make a skill harder to select?

options.text: Every included responsibility makes the skill equally suitable for each task
options.feedback: Listing many kinds of work does not establish equal suitability. Unrelated responsibilities can make its intended use less clear.

options.text: A broader skill can be selected without considering its description
options.feedback: The description still supplies the initial selection guidance. Breadth does not remove the need to assess relevance.

options.text: More responsibilities reduce the importance of the requested outcome
options.feedback: The requested outcome remains the basis for choosing a procedure. A broad collection of instructions cannot replace that match.

options.text: Unrelated responsibilities make the skill's intended use less distinct
options.feedback: A focused procedure is easier to match to a concrete task. Unrelated responsibilities blur the boundary of what the skill handles.
